headline: Drones reach civilians on beach and market
deck: Russian officials report deaths after a drone descends on a Krasnodar beach while Ukrainian police video captures an FPV pursuit of a Kherson market seller, leaving mechanism and attribution unresolved.
body: Two distinct drone incidents on successive days left civilians dead or wounded in places lacking confirmed military presence at the moment of impact. Russian regional authorities reported casualties after a drone came down among beachgoers at Arkhipo-Osipovka in Krasnodar Krai on 3 August.[E1] The following day Ukrainian police released footage of an FPV drone pursuing a market vendor in Kherson.[E4] The shared feature is the demonstrated reach of current drone systems into spaces occupied by non-combatants.

Krasnodar officials ultimately reported seven people killed, including three children.[E1] The BBC’s verification also recorded gunfire before the explosion, while the exact impact mechanism remained unclear.[E1] Governor Veniamin Kondratyev characterised the event as a deliberate strike, yet no independent forensic reconstruction has settled the question of intent or exact flight path.

Verified footage showed a drone heading toward the beach before an explosion, with gunfire audible beforehand.[E1] CNN’s video analysis found automatic gunfire from several weapons and a sharp change in the drone’s path before impact.[E2] These acoustic and trajectory indicators leave open competing accounts of direct strike versus interception, and the public record does not resolve which explanation holds.

Ukrainian police footage showed a drone pursuing a market vendor around a van before exploding nearby; the 52-year-old survived with blast and shrapnel injuries.[E4] President Zelenskyy posted the police video and said the Kherson vegetable seller was wounded in the blast.[E3] The visual sequence establishes low-altitude pursuit and detonation in a civilian commercial setting without independently confirming operator identity or rules of engagement.

Attribution of the Kherson FPV rests on Ukrainian official statements and geography rather than technical linkage of the specific airframe. The beach case similarly leaves mechanism contested between the reported gunfire, path change and official characterisation of a deliberate attack.[E1][E2] Neither episode supplies a settled finding of intentional civilian targeting on the available public evidence.

The two events remain separate in time, location, platform and claimed authorship. What they share is the capacity of small and longer-range drones to place non-combatants in the path of effects, whether by design, interception or proximity. All casualty figures and visual descriptions remain those of the named public sources cited here.[E1][E3][E4]

evidence_box.fragment: “A drone hit a busy beach in southern Russia, killing seven people including three children.”
“automatic gunfire from at least three weapons is audible”
“A Russian drone deliberately hunted down a man selling vegetables”
“The video shows the man running around the van from which he was selling his goods”

art.caption: The beach strike near Arkhipo-Osipovka and the Kherson market pursuit sit on opposite sides of the same drone war.
